138|## Deployment (btrfs send/receive)
139|
140|**Owner clarification (2026-09-13): there is no deployment script. Deployment
141|is btrfs send/receive of the prepared filesystem snapshot.** The release
142|boundary is the snapshot's contents and the send/receive transfer. Existing
143|`deploy/` scripts are source/history or preparation tooling; neither
144|`build-golden.sh` nor `btrfs-layout.sh` defines the current deployment mechanism.
145|Never hand-copy binaries onto a running host as a deploy step.
146|
147|**Owner decision (2026-10-14): `./activate-golden.sh` at the repo root is the one
148|command for deploying a new version.** It runs the internal
149|`deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh` helper, then `op-release-launch release`:
150|btrfs send/receive of a golden snapshot into the inactive of two slots, then a
151|live read-only overlay swap at `/opt/op-dbus/current` (active + previous only;
152|`op-release-launch rollback` undoes it). The 2026-09-13 "no deployment script"
153|rule above is superseded for this entry point; the transport is still send/receive.
154|
155|`deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh` only populates and validates
156|`/opt/op-dbus/golden` from already built artifacts and an already sealed,
157|persisted catalog. Set `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE` to use an isolated release
158|catalog; the script validates and copies it but never reseals it. It does not
159|create the read-only release snapshot, send
160|or receive it, activate a received filesystem, install files into the running
161|host, or restart services. `--golden-only` remains a compatibility alias for
162|its default behavior; the former `--live-only` and `--no-restart` modes are
163|retired. Snapshot creation, `btrfs send/receive`, target activation, and any
164|deliberate target service action are separate operator steps.

166|```sh
167|CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
168|sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm            # explicitly reseal after the build
169|sudo target/release/opblob persist             # retain the catalog across reboot
170|```
171|
172|After builds, explicitly run the freshly built `opblob` to seal the release catalog; bridge startup only consumes sealed blobs and never reseals. For isolated release preparation, use `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>` and pass that catalog as `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; publishing live SHM remains part of activation. Match the service's schema-shaping environment. The renamed cognitive code reads `COGNITIVE_*`: `COGNITIVE_QDRANT_URL` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:6334`, matching the current `deploy/runit/op-grpc-bridge/run`; the historical `COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL=http://10.200.0.2:6334` instruction is obsolete. 299|## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants (read these before touching plugins, state, or identity)
300|
301|- **Identity storage lifecycle (owner correction 2026-10-05).** Cozo owns identity-to-leaf/loop assignment and isolation. One immutable physical seed is shared through read-only views; each identity keeps its own writable leaf and the existing seven subvolumes. Only the external host provisioner may add a new blank leaf once, during explicit creation. Login, start, stop, logout, restart, bridge recovery and failed-start cleanup must NEVER add/remove Btrfs members. Start verifies/remounts the existing pair through the host mount owner; stop leaves membership and data intact. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage and records logical attachment. Do not interpret `attached=false` as device removal. No root copies, snapshots, new subvolumes or OverlayFS fallback during identity provisioning. Never modify a seed while retained leaves depend on it. Older add-on-start/remove-on-stop guidance in source, handoffs and signals is superseded; do not restore it. Host release snapshot/send/receive below is a separate deployment mechanism.
302|- **D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`. No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops in plugin/service code. New backend capabilities register as plugins in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs` — never as new gRPC proto service packages.
303|- **The plugin IS the schema — one source of truth, nonnegotiable.** That single schema is sealed into the blob, which IS the plugin. D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from it. Validate inputs against it. Each plugin defines its schema under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, using `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`. **There must be no parallel plugin schema source in a repository-level or plugin `schemas/` directory.** The former plugin capture directories, separate section files, and JSON-file loader have been removed. `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_loader.rs` still exists by name, but it reads only a manifest-pinned `PluginSchema` from the sealed blob catalog; it is not a file-schema fallback. **Owner correction (2026-10-18): capture threetched's full `config schema` from the verified binary on every seal.** The shared capture fixes the runtime config directory, checks the binary and manifest, and supplies native_config, MCP, model_routes, plugins and skill_bundles. `tched_router_contract.rs` contains only access/section helpers; the embedded UPSTREAM IMPORT is retired. Build-time generated bridge contracts explicitly prepare the same capture; runtime consumes the sealed catalog and never starts capture as a fallback. Do not restore an embedded schema or add independent captures using the sealer's ambient environment. The per-section generator and generated surface were retired on 2026-10-04. Older docs claiming a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` are also stale — that file does not exist.
304|- **The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob`. A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob`. Consumers read SHM directly (zero-copy) — they never re-hash and never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder and `live-schema.json` are gone.
305|- **MutationEngine owns state; streaming comes from SHM (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** MutationEngine folds authoritative backend results into the complete state tree, including child objects, and commits that state to canonical SHM before change notifications. Child updates/deletions must preserve unrelated children and parent fields. Existing subscriptions derive their values from committed SHM; an in-memory event payload, method argument, or generator buffer is not a second state authority. Preserve verified principal/session scope for private state. Do not add a separate per-method streaming control plane or claim a buffered unary response provides state streaming.
306|- **MCP gateway (settled).** One public MCP door: `:8090` on `op-grpc-bridge` (cognitive MCP is in-process there; no standalone `op-cognitive-mcp` runit service). `compact_mcp` is a retired plugin id. Compact *mode* (4 meta-tools) is in-process in op-web for the singleton control-plane chatbot; it is not an MCP plugin and not a second listener. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.
307|- **External binaries back plugins; the plugin remains the single schema source.** 3tched-router / tched-router (`tched_router` in code) is the framework/schema/plugin integration backed by the autonomous `/usr/bin/threetched` executable. The reproducible threetched input is pinned in `vendor/tched-router/source.pin`; `vendor/tched-router/build-threetched.sh` applies the checked-in patches and emits `target/threetched-artifacts/tched-router/{threetched,manifest.json}` without installing it. `build-golden.sh` validates the pin, patch and binary provenance, then stages the binary, `/usr/share/op-dbus/threetched-manifests/tched-router.json`, `/etc/op-dbus/threetched-runtime.toml`, and the tracked default skill bundle into the golden filesystem. The `tched-router` runit service verifies that manifest, exact commit, binary digest, and version before exec, then seeds its private runtime config and skills from those staged bootstrap files. A fresh checkout includes the digest-pinned upstream source archive, patches and build recipe; the helper verifies and uses that archive by default. Cargo registry dependencies and system build tools still need provisioning. Owner correction (2026-10-11): the executable and runtime-facing branding are lowercase `threetched`; the FUSE discovery source is `threetched-surface.rs`. {'content': '1|---\n2|name: btrfs\n3|description: >\n4|  Btrfs filesystem administration: subvolumes, snapshots, rollback, balance,\n5|  scrub, RAID profiles, compression, quotas, send/receive backups, and\n6|  troubleshooting.\n7|  MUST consult when installing, configuring, or troubleshooting btrfs.\n8|triggerPhrases:\n9|  - "btrfs"\n10|  - "Btrfs"\n11|  - "btrfs snapshot"\n12|  - "btrfs subvolume"\n13|  - "btrfs balance"\n14|  - "btrfs scrub"\n15|  - "copy-on-write filesystem"\n16|  - "CoW filesystem"\n17|  - "btrfs-progs"\n18|  - "mkfs.btrfs"\n19|  - "snapper"\n20|  - "btrbk"\n21|globs:\n22|  - "**/fstab"\n23|  - "**/etc/fstab"\n24|last_verified: "unverified"\n25|---\n26|\n27|## Identity\n28|\n29|| Property | Value |\n30||----------|-------|\n31|| **Type** | Kernel built-in filesystem (no loadable module needed on most distros) |\n32|| **CLI tool** | `btrfs` (subcommands: `filesystem`, `subvolume`, `balance`, `scrub`, `device`, `quota`, `qgroup`, `check`, `defragment`, `rescue`) |\n33|| **Distro install** | `apt install btrfs-progs` / `dnf install btrfs-progs` |\n34|| **Create** | `mkfs.btrfs` |\n35|| **Kernel version matters** | Significant stability improvements landed between 4.x and 6.x; older kernels have known bugs with RAID-5/6 and balance |\n36|\n37|## Quick Start\n38|\n39|```bash\n40|sudo apt install btrfs-progs\n41|sudo mkfs.btrfs -L mydata /dev/sdX1\n42|sudo mount /dev/sdX1 /mnt/mydata\n43|btrfs filesystem show /mnt/mydata\n44|btrfs device stats /mnt/mydata\n45|```\n46|\n47|## Key Operations\n48|\n49|| Task | Command |\n50||------|---------|\n51|| Show filesystems | `btrfs filesystem show` |\n52|| Filesystem usage (detailed) | `btrfs filesystem usage /mount` |\n53|| List subvolumes | `btrfs subvolume list /mount` |\n54|| Create subvolume | `btrfs subvolume create /mount/name` |\n55|| Delete subvolume | `btrfs subvolume delete /mount/name` |\n56|| Create read-write snapshot | `btrfs subvolume snapshot /mount/src /mount/dst` |\n57|| Create read-only snapshot | `btrfs subvolume snapshot -r /mount/src /mount/dst` |\n58|| Rollback: delete current, rename snapshot | `btrfs subvolume delete /mount/@; mv /mount/@snapshot /mount/@` |\n59|| Rollback: recreate subvolume from snapshot | `btrfs subvolume snapshot /mount/@snapshot /mount/@` |\n60|| Balance start (all chunks) | `btrfs balance start /mount` |\n61|| Balance start (metadata only) | `btrfs balance start -mconvert=raid1 /mount` |\n62|| Balance status | `btrfs balance status /mount` |\n63|| Balance cancel | `btrfs balance cancel /mount` |\n64|| Scrub start | `btrfs scrub start /mount` |\n65|| Scrub status | `btrfs scrub status /mount` |\n66|| Scrub cancel | `btrfs scrub cancel /mount` |\n67|| Check filesystem (read-only) | `btrfs check /dev/sdX` (unmounted) |\n68|| Defragment file or directory | `btrfs filesystem defragment -r /mount` |\n69|| Resize (grow) | `btrfs filesystem resize max /mount` |\n70|| Resize (shrink) | `btrfs filesystem resize -10G /mount` |\n71|| Add device | `btrfs device add /dev/sdY /mount` |\n72|| Remove device | `btrfs device remove /dev/sdY /mount` |\n73|| Device read/write error stats | `btrfs device stats /mount` |\n74|| Enable quotas | `btrfs quota enable /mount` |\n75|| Show qgroup usage | `btrfs qgroup show -reF /mount` |\n76|\n77|## Expected State\n78|\n79|- `btrfs device stats /mount` → all counters are `0` (any non-zero value is a read/write error)\n80|- `btrfs scrub status /mount` → `Status: finished` with `0 errors`\n81|- `btrfs balance status /mount` → `No balance found on \'/mount\'` when idle\n82|- `btrfs filesystem usage /mount` → Data and metadata ratios show reasonable allocation (metadata should not be >80% full)\n83|\n84|## Health Checks\n85|\n86|1. `btrfs device stats /mount` → all counters `0`; any non-zero value means hardware errors, act immediately\n87|2. `btrfs filesystem usage /mount` → check both Data and Metadata sections; metadata ENOSPC is the most common silent failure\n88|3. `btrfs scrub status /mount` → verify last scrub completed with no errors; schedule scrubs monthly via systemd timer or cron\n89|4. `btrfs subvolume list /mount` → audit snapshot count; accumulation fills disk without appearing in normal `df` output\n90|\n91|## Common Failures\n92|\n93|| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n94||---------|-------|-----|\n95|| `no space left on device` but `df` shows free space | Metadata chunks exhausted while data chunks exist | `btrfs filesystem usage /mount` — run `btrfs balance start -dusage=50 /mount` to rebalance underused chunks |\n96|| RAID-1 on data but single on metadata | Dangerous default when adding a second disk; metadata is not redundant | `btrfs filesystem usage /mount` — check metadata profile; run `btrfs balance start -mconvert=raid1 /mount` |\n97|| Filesystem mounts read-only | Encountered an error it cannot self-correct | Check `dmesg | grep -i btrfs`; run `btrfs check /dev/sdX` on unmounted device to assess damage |\n98|| Balance fails with ENOSPC mid-run | Not enough free space to relocate all chunks | Use `-dusage=<N>` filter to relocate only partially-used chunks first; free up space before retrying |\n99|| Qgroup show reports inflated usage | Qgroups track snapshot references — shared data counted in each | Shared data is expected; use `btrfs qgroup show -reF` to see exclusive vs shared bytes |\n100|| Snapshot accumulation fills disk | Old snapshots reference deleted data, preventing space reclaim | `btrfs subvolume list /mount | grep snapshot` — delete old snapshots with `btrfs subvolume delete` |\n101|| `btrfs check --repair` made it worse | `--repair` is not safe for general use and can corrupt data | Never run `--repair` without consulting upstream; use `rescue` subcommands instead |\n102|| Filesystem errors after kernel upgrade | Older on-disk format or regression | Check `dmesg`; downgrade kernel or use `btrfs rescue` tools; check known issues for your kernel version |\n103|\n104|## Pain Points\n105|\n106|- **ENOSPC due to metadata/data imbalance**: The most common Btrfs "gotcha". Btrfs allocates space in chunks — if metadata chunks fill up, writes fail even when data chunks are available and `df` still shows free space. Fix: `btrfs balance start -dusage=50 /mount` to reclaim partially-empty chunks. This is not a bug — it is the expected behavior when chunk allocation becomes imbalanced.\n107|- **Mixed RAID profiles between data and metadata**: Adding a second disk does not automatically mirror metadata. A system can have `RAID1` data but `single` metadata, meaning metadata loss on one disk is fatal. Always explicitly set both with `-d` and `-m` flags.\n108|- **Snapshots are instant but they accumulate**: Snapshot creation is O(1) and free. Deletion requires reference counting and can be slow. Unreferenced snapshots hold on to deleted data indefinitely — disk usage only decreases after snapshot deletion completes.\n109|- **`btrfs check` is slow and `--repair` is risky**: Unlike `fsck.ext4`, Btrfs check does not have a safe repair mode. `--repair` can corrupt a filesystem that `check` reports as damaged. Prefer `btrfs rescue` subcommands (`zero-log`, `fix-device-size`) for targeted fixes.\n110|- **Btrfs RAID-5/6 has known parity issues**: As of kernels through 6.x, Btrfs RAID-5 and RAID-6 have unresolved write-hole bugs. Do not use RAID-5/6 for data you care about. Use RAID-1 or RAID-10 instead.\n111|- **Send/receive for backups**: `btrfs send` / `btrfs receive` is efficient for incremental backups using read-only snapshots as base references. Tools like `snapper` and `btrbk` automate the snapshot lifecycle and send/receive workflow — prefer them over manual scripting.\n112|- **CoW fragmentation on databases and VMs**: Copy-on-write writes new data to new locations, which fragments sequential files over time. Use `nodatacow` mount option (or `chattr +C`) for VM disk images, database files, and other large randomly-written files. `nodatacow` also disables checksums for those files.\n113|\n114|## See Also\n115|\n116|- **ext4** — Traditional Linux filesystem without CoW overhead; use when you need maximum compatibility and don\'t need snapshots\n117|- **xfs** — High-performance filesystem for large sequential I/O; use for databases and media workloads where CoW fragmentation is a concern\n118|- **zfs** — Full storage stack with pooling and replication; use when you need enterprise-grade checksums and send/receive without kernel version sensitivity\n119|- **lvm** — Logical volume manager; provides snapshot and resize capabilities at the block layer beneath btrfs\n120|\n121|## References\n122|\n123|See `references/` for:\n124|- `btrfs-options.md` — mkfs and mount options organized by category\n125|- `common-patterns.md` — filesystem setup, subvolume layouts, snapshots, rollback, backup, RAID, and compression\n126|- `docs.md` — official documentation and community links', 'total_lines': 126, 'file_size': 8377, 'truncated': False, 'is_binary': False, 'is_image': False, 'not_found': False}

{'content': '1|---\n2|name: rust-memory-optimization\n3|description: |\n4|  Memory optimization and allocation reduction in Rust. Use when:\n5|  - User is designing memory-sensitive or low-latency systems\n6|  - Optimizing data structures to reduce memory footprint\n7|  - Replacing heap allocations with stack-allocated/bounded structures (SmallVec, ArrayVec, ThinVec)\n8|  - Handling small strings with optimizations (CompactString)\n9|  - Reusing collections via clear() in loops\n10|  - Implementing zero-copy decoding and references\n11|  - Structuring arena-allocated memory (Bumpalo)\n12|  - Measuring memory usage, profiling heap, or diagnosing leaks\n13|---\n14|\n15|\n16|\n17|## Quick Navigation\n18|\n19|- [references/stack_allocations.md](references/stack_allocations.md)\n20|- [references/arenas.md](references/arenas.md)\n21|\n22|# Rust Memory Optimization Guide\n23|\n24|Advanced strategies for reducing allocations, shrinking layout sizes, and boosting performance.\n25|\n26|## Core Rules & Patterns\n27|\n28|### 1. Bounded Heap-Free Collections\n29|For collections that are usually small, avoid standard vectors to bypass heap allocations.\n30|- **`SmallVec`**: Stack-allocated up to a threshold, overflows to the heap.\n31|- **`ArrayVec`**: Fixed-capacity array wrapper; never allocates on the heap.\n32|- **`ThinVec`**: Only takes a single pointer size when empty, reducing size in enum layouts.\n33|\n34|```rust\n35|use smallvec::{smallvec, SmallVec};\n36|use arrayvec::ArrayVec;\n37|\n38|// SmallVec: Allocates 4 items on the stack. Goes to heap only if count > 4.\n39|let mut local_tags: SmallVec<[String; 4]> = smallvec![];\n40|local_tags.push("Rust".to_string());\n41|\n42|// ArrayVec: Absolute limit of 8 items on the stack. No heap overflow.\n43|let mut coordinates: ArrayVec<f64, 8> = ArrayVec::new();\n44|coordinates.push(42.0);\n45|```\n46|\n47|### 2. Small String Optimization (SSO)\n48|Standard `String` consumes 24 bytes and allocates heap space immediately. Use `CompactString` for inline small strings (under 24 bytes) without allocating.\n49|\n50|```rust\n51|use compact_str::CompactString;\n52|\n53|// No heap allocation for strings <= 24 characters\n54|let username = CompactString::new("user_123");\n55|```\n56|\n57|### 3. Boxed Slices vs Vectors\n58|If a collection\'s size is determined once at initialization and never changes, convert it from `Vec<T>` to `Box<[T]>` to save 8 bytes of stack capacity space.\n59|\n60|```rust\n61|let items_vec: Vec<i32> = vec![1, 2, 3];\n62|\n63|// Save capacity field (shrinks stack representation from 24 to 16 bytes)\n64|let items_slice: Box<[i32]> = items_vec.into_boxed_slice();\n65|```\n66|\n67|### 4. Zero-Copy Patterns\n68|Instead of cloning or allocating strings, hold references to existing memory using slices or crates like `bytes::Bytes`.\n69|\n70|```rust\n71|use bytes::Bytes;\n72|\n73|pub struct Message {\n74|    // Zero-copy reference-counted byte buffer slice\n75|    pub payload: Bytes,\n76|}\n77|\n78|// Can be sliced and shared among threads without cloning underlying memory\n79|let original = Bytes::from(vec![0; 1024]);\n80|let slice = original.slice(0..100); \n81|```\n82|\n83|### 5. Arena Allocation\n84|For batch allocation where structures share a lifecycle (e.g. AST parsing), use arena allocators (`bumpalo`) to allocate items sequentially in a continuous region of memory and free them all at once.\n85|\n86|```rust\n87|use bumpalo::Bump;\n88|\n89|let bump = Bump::new();\n90|\n91|// Allocates quickly on the bump arena\n92|let string_ref = bump.alloc_str("dynamic string");\n93|let int_ref = bump.alloc(42);\n94|\n95|// Entire arena is cleared at once on drop\n96|```\n97|\n98|### 6. Collection Reuse\n99|Reuse collection allocations in performance-critical loops with `.clear()` instead of re-instantiating.\n100|\n101|```rust\n102|// Bad: Allocates a new vector every iteration\n103|for item in feed {\n104|    let mut batch = Vec::new();\n105|    batch.push(item);\n106|}\n107|\n108|// Good: Reuses allocation buffer\n109|let mut batch = Vec::with_capacity(100);\n110|for item in feed {\n111|    batch.clear();\n112|    batch.push(item);\n113|}\n114|```\n115|\n116|## Layout Awareness\n117|\n118|Use `std::mem::size_of` to understand data layout.\n119|\n120|```rust\n121|println!("User size: {}", std::mem::size_of::<User>());\n122|```\n123|\n124|Reorder fields to reduce padding only when the type is numerous or hot.\n125|\n126|```rust\n127|// Often smaller: group large-alignment fields first\n128|struct Record {\n129|    id: u64,\n130|    flags: u32,\n131|    kind: u8,\n132|}\n133|```\n134|\n135|## String Strategy\n136|\n137|```rust\n138|fn label<\'a>(name: &\'a str, fallback: &\'a str) -> std::borrow::Cow<\'a, str> {\n139|    if name.is_empty() { fallback.into() } else { name.into() }\n140|}\n141|```\n142|\n143|Avoid `format!` in tight loops. Reuse buffers with `clear()`.\n144|\n145|## Zero-Copy Parsing\n146|\n147|Return slices into the input when the input outlives parsed data.\n148|\n149|```rust\n150|pub struct Header<\'a> {\n151|    pub name: &\'a str,\n152|    pub value: &\'a str,\n153|}\n154|```\n155|\n156|Do not force zero-copy when it creates unmanageable lifetimes for little gain.\n157|\n158|## ThinVec for Enum Payloads\n159|\n160|When enums contain `Vec` variants, `ThinVec` reduces the enum size by storing only a pointer when empty:\n161|\n162|```rust\n163|use thin_vec::ThinVec;\n164|\n165|// Regular Vec in an enum makes the enum 24+ bytes even when empty\n166|enum Node {\n167|    Leaf(i64),\n168|    Children(Vec<Node>),     // 24 bytes for Vec\n169|}\n170|\n171|// ThinVec only stores 8 bytes (a pointer) when empty\n172|enum NodeOptimized {\n173|    Leaf(i64),\n174|    Children(ThinVec<Node>), // 8 bytes for ThinVec\n175|}\n176|```\n177|\n178|## Cow for Conditional Ownership\n179|\n180|```rust\n181|use std::borrow::Cow;\n182|\n183|pub struct Error {\n184|    message: Cow<\'static, str>,\n185|}\n186|\n187|impl Error {\n188|    // No allocation for static messages\n189|    pub fn new(msg: &\'static str) -> Self {\n190|        Self { message: Cow::Borrowed(msg) }\n191|    }\n192|\n193|    // Allocates only when dynamic\n194|    pub fn with_detail(msg: String) -> Self {\n195|        Self { message: Cow::Owned(msg) }\n196|    }\n197|}\n198|```\n199|\n200|## Arc vs Rc Trade-offs\n201|\n202|```rust\n203|use std::rc::Rc;\n204|use std::sync::Arc;\n205|\n206|// Single-threaded shared ownership — cheaper than Arc\n207|let shared = Rc::new(large_data);\n208|\n209|// Multi-threaded shared ownership — required across threads\n210|let shared = Arc::new(large_data);\n211|```\n212|\n213|Prefer `Rc` when data never crosses thread boundaries. `Arc` adds atomic reference counting overhead.\n214|\n215|## HashMap Memory Optimization\n216|\n217|```rust\n218|use hashbrown::HashMap;\n219|\n220|// hashbrown\'s HashMap uses less memory than std\'s and is faster\n221|let mut map: HashMap<String, i32> = HashMap::with_capacity(128);\n222|\n223|// Reserve capacity upfront to avoid rehashing\n224|map.reserve(expected_count);\n225|\n226|// Consider FxHashMap for non-adversarial keys\n227|use 2|//! come from one root-owned, digest-pinned plan, never from method arguments.
3|//! The absent-record Cozo journal fences uncertain storage/Incus effects.
4|

14|const PROVISION_CAPABILITY: &str = "identity_sled.write";

17|#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
18|pub(super) struct ProvisionInput {

20|    pub plan_sha256: String,
21|}

24|#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
25|struct SeedProvisionPlan {
26|    version: u8,
27|    session_id: String,
28|    wireguard_pubkey: String,
29|    expected_revision: u64,
30|    expected_revision_operation_id: String,
31|    seed_image_path: String,
32|    seed_sha256: String,
33|    seed_fsid: String,
34|    new_leaf_image_path: String,
35|    leaf_size_bytes: u64,
36|    mount_point: String,
37|    pool_name: String,
38|    image_fingerprint: String,
39|    instance: IncusInstance,
40|}
41|
42|fn normalized_absolute(path: &str) -> bool {
43|    Path::new(path).is_absolute()
44|        && Path::new(path)
45|            .components()
46|            .all(|part| matches!(part, Component::RootDir | Component::Normal(_)))
47|}
48|
49|impl SeedProvisionPlan {
50|    fn pool_source(&self) -> PathBuf {
51|        Path::new(&self.mount_point).join("pool")
52|    }
53|    fn persist_source(&self) -> PathBuf {
54|        Path::new(&self.mount_point).join("persist")
55|    }
56|
57|    fn validate(&self, input: &ProvisionInput, expected: &IdentityRevision) -> Result<()> {
58|        anyhow::ensure!(self.version == 1, "unsupported seed provision plan version");
59|        let key_bytes = base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD
60|            .decode(&input.wireguard_pubkey)
61|            .context("invalid provision public key encoding")?;
62|        anyhow::ensure!(
63|            key_bytes.len() == 32
64|                && base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(&key_bytes)
65|                    == input.wireguard_pubkey,
66|            "provision public key is not canonical 32-byte Base64"
67|        );
68|        anyhow::ensure!(
69|            self.wireguard_pubkey == input.wireguard_pubkey
70|                && self.session_id
71|                    == op_identity::session::derive_session_id(&input.wireguard_pubkey)
72|                && expected.session_id == self.session_id
73|                && expected.revision == self.expected_revision
74|                && expected.operation_id == self.expected_revision_operation_id
75|                && expected.record.is_none()
76|                && expected.genesis.is_none(),
77|            "trusted seed provision plan does not match the absent identity"
78|        );
79|        anyhow::ensure!(
80|            super::root_repair::valid_digest(&self.seed_sha256)
81|                && super::root_repair::valid_digest(&self.image_fingerprint)
82|                && uuid::Uuid::parse_str(&self.seed_fsid).is_ok()
83|                && self.leaf_size_bytes >= 1024 * 1024 * 1024,
84|            "invalid sealed seed or image provenance"
85|        );
86|        for path in [
87|            &self.seed_image_path,
88|            &self.new_leaf_image_path,
89|            &self.mount_point,
90|        ] {
91|            anyhow::ensure!(normalized_absolute(path), "noncanonical provision path");
92|        }
93|        op_plugins::state_plugins::incus::validate_root_repair_pool_name(&self.pool_name)?;
94|        anyhow::ensure!(
95|            self.instance.name == self.session_id
96|                && self.instance.instance_type == "container"
97|                && self.instance.status == "Stopped"
98|                && self.instance.image.as_deref() == Some(self.image_fingerprint.as_str())
99|                && self.instance.storage_pool.as_deref() == Some(self.pool_name.as_str())
100|                && self.instance.profiles == ["identity"],
101|            "seeded instance identity, image, pool or profile differs from plan"
102|        );
103|        let config = self
104|            .instance
105|            .config
106|            .as_ref()
107|            .context("seeded instance config absent")?;
108|        anyhow::ensure!(
109|            config.get("boot.autostart").map(String::as_str) == Some("false")
110|                && config.get("security.privileged").map(String::as_str) == Some("false")
111|                && config.get("security.nesting").map(String::as_str) == Some("false")
112|                && !config.keys().any(|key| key.starts_with("volatile.")
113|                    || key.starts_with("raw.")
114|                    || key.starts_with("image.")),
115|            "seeded instance is not parked and unprivileged"
116|        );
117|        anyhow::ensure!(
118|            self.instance
119|                .devices
120|                .iter()
121|                .all(|named| matches!(named.device, Device::Disk(_)))
122|                && self
123|                    .instance
124|                    .expanded_devices
125|                    .iter()
126|                    .all(|named| matches!(named.device, Device::Disk(_)))
127|                && self.instance.expanded_config.is_some(),
128|            "seeded instance includes untrusted local devices"
129|        );
130|        let devices = self
131|            .instance
132|            .devices
133|            .iter()
134|            .map(|named| (named.name.as_str(), named.device.to_incus_map()))
135|            .collect::<std::collections::BTreeMap<_, _>>();
136|        anyhow::ensure!(
137|            devices.len() == self.instance.devices.len(),
138|            "duplicate seeded device"
139|        );
140|        let root = devices.get("root").context("seeded root disk absent")?;
141|        let persist = devices
142|            .get("persist")
143|            .context("seeded persist disk absent")?;
144|        anyhow::ensure!(
145|            root.get("type").map(String::as_str) == Some("disk")
146|                && root.get("path").map(String::as_str) == Some("/")
147|                && root.get("pool").map(String::as_str) == Some(self.pool_name.as_str())
148|                && root.len() == 3
149|                && persist.get("type").map(String::as_str) == Some("disk")
150|                && persist.get("path").map(String::as_str) == Some("/opt/run-mounts/persist")
151|                && persist.get("source").map(String::as_str) == self.persist_source().to_str()
152|                && persist.get("shift").map(String::as_str) == Some("true")
153|                && persist.len() == 4
154|                && devices.keys().all(|name| matches!(
155|                    *name,
156|                    "root" | "persist" | "identity" | "ghostbridge-socket"
157|                )),
158|            "seeded root or shifted persistence differs from trusted plan"
159|        );
160|        let expanded = super::root_repair::projected_devices(&self.instance, true)?;
161|        let expanded_config = self
162|            .instance
163|            .expanded_config
164|            .as_ref()
165|            .context("trusted profile config absent")?;
166|        anyhow::ensure!(
167|            expanded
168|                .get("root")
169|                .is_some_and(|root| root["pool"] == self.pool_name)
170|                && expanded
171|                    .get("persist")
172|                    .is_some_and(|persist| persist["source"]
173|                        == self.persist_source().to_string_lossy().as_ref()
174|                        && persist["shift"] == "true")
175|                && !expanded.values().any(|device| device["type"] == "nic")
176|                && expanded.keys().all(|name| matches!(
177|                    name.as_str(),
178|                    "root" | "persist" | "identity" | "ghostbridge-socket"
179|                ))
180|                && expanded_config.get("boot.autostart").map(String::as_str) == Some("false")
181|                && expanded_config
182|                    .get("security.privileged")
183|                    .map(String::as_str)
184|                    == Some("false")
185|                && !expanded_config.keys().any(|key| key.starts_with("raw.")
186|                    || key.starts_with("volatile.")
187|                    || key.starts_with("image.")),
188|            "trusted profile expansion is not the pinned disk-only layout"
189|        );
190|        Ok(())
191|    }

194|fn verify_creation_config(
195|    expected: &std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
196|    observed: &std::collections::HashMap<String, String>,
197|) -> Result<()> {
198|    let mut observed = observed.clone();
199|    // Incus adds these while creating a stopped unprivileged container. Keep
200|    // the set closed and check their shape before accepting the native
201|    // readback; the full values are then retained in authoritative state.
202|    for key in [
203|        "volatile.uuid.generation",
204|        "volatile.cloud-init.instance-id",
205|    ] {
206|        if let Some(value) = observed.remove(key) {
207|            anyhow::ensure!(
208|                uuid::Uuid::parse_str(&value).is_ok_and(|uuid| uuid.to_string() == value),
209|                "native create added an invalid Incus UUID field"
210|            );
211|        }
212|    }
213|    if let Some(value) = observed.remove("volatile.idmap.base") {
214|        anyhow::ensure!(
215|            value.parse::<u64>().is_ok(),
216|            "native create added an invalid Incus idmap base"
217|        );
218|    }
219|    if let Some(value) = observed.remove("volatile.last_state.idmap") {
220|        anyhow::ensure!(
221|            serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&value).is_ok_and(|json| json.is_array()),
222|            "native create added an invalid Incus prior idmap"
223|        );
224|    }
225|    for key in [
226|        "volatile.uuid",
227|        "volatile.base_image",
228|        "volatile.idmap.next",
229|        "volatile.apply_template",
230|        "volatile.last_state.power",
231|        "volatile.last_state.ready",
232|    ] {
233|        observed.remove(key);
234|    }
235|    // These descriptive fields come from the pinned image metadata, rather
236|    // than the create request. The exact base-image fingerprint is checked
237|    // separately before this comparison.
238|    observed.retain(|key, _| !key.starts_with("image."));
239|    anyhow::ensure!(
240|        !observed.keys().any(|key| key.starts_with("volatile.")) && &observed == expected,
241|        "native create added or changed unpinned configuration"
242|    );
243|    Ok(())
244|}

{"content":"1|//! Atomic fresh same-key adoption. History is private and never projected into the new record.
2|use super::*;
3|
4|pub struct IdentityCleanProvision {
5|    pub expected: IdentityRevision,
6|    pub record: IdentitySledRecord,
7|    pub genesis: GenesisInputsRecord,
8|    pub plan_sha256: String,
9|    pub provenance_json: String,
10|}
11|
12|#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
13|pub struct CleanProvisionReceipt {
14|    pub plan_sha256: String,
15|    pub operation_id: String,
16|    pub expected_revision: u64,
17|    pub committed_revision: u64,
18|    pub provenance_json: String,
19|    pub btrfs_device_json: String,
20|    pub instance_json: String,
21|}
22|
23|fn read(
24|    tx: &MultiTransaction,
25|    sid: &str,
26|) -> std::result::Result<Option<CleanProvisionReceipt>, CozoError> {
27|    let rows = query(
28|        tx,
29|        "?[committed_revision,plan_sha256,operation_id,expected_revision,provenance_json,btrfs_device_json,instance_json] := *identity_clean_provisions{session_id,committed_revision,plan_sha256,operation_id,expected_revision,provenance_json,btrfs_device_json,instance_json}, session_id = $sid :order -committed_revision :limit 1",
30|        sid_params(sid),
31|    )?;
32|    let row = match rows.rows.as_slice() {
33|        [] => return Ok(None),
34|        [row] if row.len() == 7 => row,
35|        _ => return Err(err("corrupt clean provision receipt")),
36|    };
37|    let receipt = CleanProvisionReceipt {
38|        committed_revision: integer(row, 0)? as u64,
39|        plan_sha256: string(row, 1)?,
40|        operation_id: string(row, 2)?,
41|        expected_revision: integer(row, 3)? as u64,
42|        provenance_json: string(row, 4)?,
43|        btrfs_device_json: string(row, 5)?,
44|        instance_json: string(row, 6)?,
45|    };
46|    if !valid_root_repair_digest(&receipt.plan_sha256)
47|        || receipt.operation_id != format!("clean-provision-{}", receipt.plan_sha256)
48|        || receipt.expected_revision.checked_add(1) != Some(receipt.committed_revision)
49|        || receipt.provenance_json.len() > 32768
50|    {
51|        return Err(err("corrupt clean provision receipt identity"));
52|    }
53|    Ok(Some(receipt))
54|}
55|
56|impl CozoGraphShuttle {
57|    pub fn read_clean_provision(
58|        &self,
59|        sid: &str,
60|    ) -> std::result::Result<Option<CleanProvisionReceipt>, CozoError> {
61|        let _guard = self
62|            .identity_transaction
63|            .lock()
64|            .map_err(|_| err("identity transaction owner is poisoned"))?;
65|        let tx = self.db.multi_transaction(false);
66|        let receipt = read(&tx, sid)?;
67|        commit_checked(&tx)?;
68|        Ok(receipt)
69|    }
70|}

72|pub(super) fn validate(
73|    tx: &MultiTransaction,
74|    sid: &str,
75|    operation: &str,
76|    previous: &IdentityRevision,
77|    metadata: &RevisionMetadata,
78|    provision: &IdentityCleanProvision,
79|) -> std::result::Result<(), CozoError> {
80|    let old = provision.expected.record.as_ref();
81|    let new = &provision.record;
82|    let explicitly_deleted = provision.expected.revision > 1
83|        && old.is_none()
84|        && provision.expected.genesis.is_none()
85|        && provision.expected.operation_id
86|            == format!("delete-provision-{sid}-{}", provision.expected.revision - 1);
87|    let provenance: Value = serde_json::from_str(&provision.provenance_json)?;
88|    let fresh_partitioned = provenance["version"] == 4
89|        && provenance["partitioned_overlay"].is_object()
90|        && provision.expected.revision == 0 && provision.expected.operation_id.is_empty()
91|        && old.is_none() && provision.expected.genesis.is_none();
92|    if !explicitly_deleted && !fresh_partitioned && old.is_none() {
93|        return Err(err(
94|            "clean provision requires an existing key or explicit deletion tombstone",
95|        ));
96|    }
97|    if !valid_root_repair_digest(&provision.plan_sha256)
98|        || operation != format!("clean-provision-{}", provision.plan_sha256)
99|        || provision.expected.session_id != sid
100|        || new.session_id != sid
101|        || old.is_some_and(|old| {
102|            old.session_id != sid || new.wireguard_pubkey != old.wireguard_pubkey
103|        })
104|        || op_identity::session::derive_session_id(&new.wireguard_pubkey) != sid
105|        || new.principal_kind.as_deref() != Some("service")
106|        || new.active
107|        || new.mutation_index != 0
108|        || new.expires_at != 0
109|        || !new.interface.is_empty()
110|        || !new.peer_ip.is_empty()
111|        || !new.vector_id.is_empty()
112|        || new.session_started_at <= 0
113|        || new.session_started_at != new.last_seen_at
114|        || new.sealed_id.is_empty()
115|        || new.session_genesis.is_empty()
116|        || new.trace_id.is_empty()
117|        || old.is_some_and(|old| {
118|            new.sealed_id == old.sealed_id
119|                || new.session_genesis == old.session_genesis
120|                || new.trace_id == old.trace_id
121|                || new.btrfs_device_json == old.btrfs_device_json
122|                || new.instance_json == old.instance_json
123|        })
124|        || provision.provenance_json.len() > 32768
125|    {
126|        return Err(err("invalid clean same-key replacement intent"));
127|    }
128|    validate_pair(sid, Some(new), Some(&provision.genesis))?;
129|    let claims =
130|        op_identity::sealed_id::SealedId::from_inline_ref(&new.sealed_id).map_err(native)?;
131|    if claims.session_id != sid
132|        || claims.wireguard_pubkey != new.wireguard_pubkey
133|        || claims.principal_id != op_identity::session::derive_principal_id(&new.wireguard_pubkey)
134|        || claims.session_genesis != new.session_genesis
135|        || claims.trace_id != new.trace_id
136|        || i64::from(claims.schema_version) != new.schema_version
137|        || claims.expires_at != 0
138|        || claims.arrival_timestamp != provision.genesis.arrival_timestamp
139|        || claims.issued_at != provision.genesis.arrival_timestamp
140|        || claims.chain_head_at_arrival != provision.genesis.chain_head_at_arrival
141|        || claims.catalog_hash_at_arrival != provision.genesis.catalog_hash_at_arrival
142|        || claims.head_timestamp_at_arrival != provision.genesis.head_timestamp_at_arrival
143|    {
144|        return Err(err(
145|            "fresh authored credential does not match clean record/genesis",
146|        ));
147|    }
148|    let device: Value = serde_json::from_str(&new.btrfs_device_json)?;
149|    let instance: Value = serde_json::from_str(&new.instance_json)?;
150|    if device["cozo_id"] != sid
151|        || device["attached"] != true
152|        || instance["status"] != "Stopped"
153|        || instance["type"] != "container"
154|        || instance["name"] != "3tchedChatbot"
155|        || !(provenance["version"] == if explicitly_deleted { 3 } else { 2 }
156|            || (provenance["version"] == 4 && (fresh_partitioned || explicitly_deleted)))
157|        || provenance["session_id"] != sid
158|        || provenance["wireguard_pubkey"] != new.wireguard_pubkey
159|    {
160|        return Err(err("invalid clean provision binding"));
161|    }
162|    if previous.operation_id == operation {
163|        let receipt =
164|            read(tx, sid)?.ok_or_else(|| err("clean provision replay receipt missing"))?;
165|        if metadata.kind != "clean-provision"
166|            || metadata.value != provision.expected.revision as i64
167|            || previous.record.as_ref() != Some(new)
168|            || previous.genesis.as_ref() != Some(&provision.genesis)
169|            || receipt.plan_sha256 != provision.plan_sha256
170|            || receipt.provenance_json != provision.provenance_json
171|        {
172|            return Err(err("clean provision operation reused for another intent"));
173|        }
174|    } else if previous != &provision.expected {
175|        return Err(err("clean provision compare/exchange conflict"));
176|    }
177|    Ok(())
178|}

180|pub(super) fn append(
181|    tx: &MultiTransaction,
182|    sid: &str,
183|    operation: &str,
184|    provision: &IdentityCleanProvision,
185|) -> std::result::Result<(), CozoError> {
186|    let revision = provision
187|        .expected
188|        .revision
189|        .checked_add(1)
190|        .filter(|v| *v <= i64::MAX as u64)
191|        .ok_or_else(|| err("identity revision overflow"))?;
192|    let root = read_root_repair_journal_in_tx(tx, sid)?;
193|    let seed = read_seed_provision_journal_in_tx(tx, sid)?;
194|    if root
195|        .as_ref()
196|        .is_some_and(|j| j.phase != "identity-committed")
197|        || seed
198|            .as_ref()
199|            .is_some_and(|j| j.phase != "identity-committed")
200|    {

203|        ));
204|    }
205|    let history = serde_json::to_string(&(root, seed, physical_root::read_in_tx(tx, sid)?))?;
206|    let params = BTreeMap::from([
207|        ("sid".into(), DataValue::Str(sid.into())),
208|        ("revision".into(), dv_int(revision as i64)),
209|        (
210|            "plan".into(),

2|//!
3|//! Uses the native Incus HTTP API over its privileged Unix socket.
4|//! Supports creating, starting, stopping, and deleting instances,
5|//! as well as profile and config management.

27|/// Top-level state representing all Incus instances on the system.
28|#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
29|#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-category" = "service"))]

31|    pub instances: Vec<IncusInstance>,
32|}

34|/// A single Incus instance, modeled on the official Incus API (`shared/api`
35|/// `Instance`/`InstancePut`).
36|///
37|/// Devices (including proxy sockets) are the typed [`NamedDevice`] union — Incus
38|/// has no first-class "socket" concept, a proxy is simply a `devices` entry with
39|/// `type: proxy`. The previous non-standard `sockets`/`IncusProxySocket` field is
40|/// gone; a container's relationship to the shared `container.sock` is resolved
41|/// by name at the projection/gemma layer, not embedded here.
42|#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
43|pub struct IncusInstance {
44|    pub name: String,
45|    /// Instance status: "Running", "Stopped", "Frozen"
46|    pub status: String,
47|    /// Instance type: "container" or "virtual-machine"
48|    #[serde(rename = "type")]
49|    pub instance_type: String,
50|    /// Numeric status code from the Incus API (read-only).
51|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
52|    pub status_code: Option<i64>,
53|    /// Source image reference, used only at creation time (`incus init <image>`).
54|    /// Not part of the official `InstancePut`; derived from config on read.
55|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
56|    pub image: Option<String>,
57|    /// Preferred storage pool used during initial creation (creation hint only).
58|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
59|    pub storage_pool: Option<String>,
60|    /// Applied profiles (e.g. ["default"])
61|    #[serde(default)]
62|    pub profiles: Vec<String>,
63|    /// Human-readable description
64|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
65|    pub description: Option<String>,
66|    /// CPU architecture (e.g. "x86_64")
67|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
68|    pub architecture: Option<String>,
69|    /// Delete instance on shutdown
70|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
71|    pub ephemeral: Option<bool>,
72|    /// Whether saved state exists on disk
73|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
74|    pub stateful: Option<bool>,
75|    /// Creation timestamp (ISO8601)
76|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
77|    pub created_at: Option<String>,
78|    /// Last start timestamp (ISO8601)
79|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
80|    pub last_used_at: Option<String>,
81|    /// Cluster member location ("none" on single-node)
82|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
83|    pub location: Option<String>,
84|    /// Incus project name
85|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
86|    pub project: Option<String>,
87|    /// Instance configuration key-value pairs (`InstancePut.config`).
88|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
89|    pub config: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
90|    /// Typed device definitions (`InstancePut.devices`). Proxy sockets, NICs,
91|    /// disks, GPUs, etc. are all variants of [`Device`].
92|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
93|    pub devices: Vec<NamedDevice>,
94|    /// Expanded (profile-merged) config, read-only (`Instance.expanded_config`).
95|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
96|    pub expanded_config: Option<HashMap<String, String>>,
97|    /// Expanded (profile-merged) devices, read-only (`Instance.expanded_devices`).
98|    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
99|    pub expanded_devices: Vec<NamedDevice>,
100|}

Implemented the coordinated Rust path; **not compiled, tested, formatted, or deployed**, as requested. `git diff --check` passed.

### Helper-facing contract

**`identity_sled.prepare_container`**
- Capability: `identity_sled.write`
- Method ID: `mut.service.identity-sled.container.prepare@v1`
- Input—unknown fields rejected:
  ```json
  {"wireguard_pubkey":"<configured chatbot public key>","operation_id":"<canonical lowercase UUID>"}
  ```
- Domain result:
  ```json
  {
    "session_id":"b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28",
    "name":"ID-N",
    "native_uuid":"<observed native UUID>",
    "operation_id":"<same UUID>",
    "phase":"complete",
    "replayed":false
  }
  ```
- MutationEngine wraps this under **`result`**.
- Retry with the **same operation ID**. Reconciliation never repeats POST, including after 404.
- Restricted to the configured, registered chatbot. Existing identity/native bindings are retained—not silently replaced.
- Requires externally configured `identity-roots` dir pool and trusted `3tched-lungs` profile; missing/mismatched prerequisites fail closed **before allocation**.
- Correct helper order: prepare container → consume returned `name` → prepare external disk → existing `provision_container` adoption. Legacy adoption remains supported.

**`incus.create_instance`**
- Required: `operation_id`.
- Optional: `source_mode` (`image` default, or `empty`), `instance_type` (`container` default), `image`, `profiles`, `config`, `devices`.
- Omit `name` or provide `""`; nonempty names are rejected.
- Result: `name`, `native_uuid`, `operation_id`, `phase`, `replayed`, `created:true`, `changes:[]`.
- **`incus.reconcile_creation`** accepts only `{"operation_id":"…"}` and returns the same shape.

### Implemented
- Durable Cozo sequence starts at `ID-1`; unresolved intent fences subsequent allocation.
- Caller/session/genesis, logical owner, schema hash and request pinned before POST.
- Exact native UUID binding, full SHM publication, then allocation finalization.
- Coordinated Incus/project creation; declarative creation fails closed.
- Identity guards resolve durable bindings/pending preparation rather than name prefixes.
- Numbered-container clean adoption and partitioned storage verification retain legacy semantics.

- `crates/op-cozo-store/src/{lib.rs,identity_transactions.rs}`
- `crates/op-cozo-store/src/identity_transactions/{native_creation.rs,clean_provision.rs}`
